_comment: RECORD, recreated 2026-09-16. This deck was built and answered on the desktop PC (DestinsLinuxPC) on 2026-09-14/15; that work was never pushed and the session continued on the Z13. The spec and answers below are copied verbatim from the session transcript. The cropped pictures and built page stayed on the desktop, and the run folders it names no longer exist, so this spec does not rebuild.

Captures then: before = the lint branch at youcoded e14feca9; after = mechanical fixes with in-between sizes rounded down; today = rounded up. Crops and boxes were computed by matching each warning's class string to its element in the screenshot.
title: Design check — the flagged spots on real screens

steps.headline: The green “connected” lights in Backup & Sync switch to the app’s own status green.
steps.changed: The status light, and the faint green tint behind a connected backup, used a stock green. They now use the same green as every other status light in the app.
steps.measured: 5 color settings on 3 lines of code
steps.notice: The green is a little softer and matches the session and project sync dots.
steps.risk: Status colors stay the same in every theme, so nothing changes between themes.

steps.path: A session on a model with a small context window → the banner above the chat
steps.headline: The amber “some rules were left out” banner switches to the app’s own warning amber.
steps.changed: The dot, border and tint used a stock amber. They now use the amber the app already uses for warnings.
steps.measured: 4 color settings on 2 lines of code
steps.notice: Almost nothing — the two ambers are within a shade of each other.

steps.headline: The project sync dots use the app’s shared green and red instead of typed-in color codes.
steps.changed: The green “synced” and red “sync error” dots were written as raw color codes. They now use the app’s shared status green and red.
steps.measured: 6 dots in 3 places; the red is identical, the green one shade lighter
steps.notice: The green dot is a touch lighter; the red one looks exactly the same.

steps.path: The model name in the status bar → Fast mode row
steps.headline: The Fast mode lightning icon turns from yellow to the app’s warning amber.
steps.changed: The icon used a stock yellow that no theme controls. The checker’s nearest match in the app’s colors is the warning amber.
steps.notice: The bolt looks orange rather than yellow.
steps.risk: Amber means “warning” elsewhere in the app, so the bolt may read as a warning.

steps.path: Projects → the project list, context files and conversations
steps.headline: Project names, file names and conversation titles sit between two text sizes. Which size should they snap to?
steps.measured: 13.5px today, in 4 places; their descriptions are 11.5px

options.label: One size smaller
pros: Lands on the 13px size Project View was signed off at
Long names fit a little better

options.label: One size larger
pros: A little easier to read at a glance
cons: Long names get cut off a bit sooner

options.label: Leave as is
pros: Nothing moves
cons: Stays off the app’s size scale, so it keeps getting flagged

steps.headline: The small folder labels under each file card sit between two text sizes. Which way should they snap?

options.label: One size smaller
pros: Keeps the labels quiet under the file names
cons: 10px is at the edge of comfortable reading

options.label: One size larger
pros: Labels become easier to read
Matches the 11px used for small labels elsewhere
cons: Labels gain a little visual weight

options.label: Leave as is
pros: Nothing moves
cons: Stays off the app’s size scale

steps.path: Projects → Context tab → the “About context” banner
steps.headline: The “About context” explanation is 12.5px, halfway between two sizes. Which should it be?

options.label: One size smaller
pros: Banner takes a little less height
cons: A paragraph of explanation gets harder to read

options.label: One size larger
pros: Matches the 13px of the rest of Project View
Easier to read a full paragraph
cons: The banner may wrap onto one more line

options.label: Leave as is
pros: Nothing moves
cons: Stays off the app’s size scale

steps.headline: The three sign-in buttons are sized by hand instead of using one of the shared button sizes. Worth fixing?

options.label: Add a large size
pros: These three look exactly the same afterwards
Any other big button can reuse the size
cons: One small decision: how big “large” is

options.label: Leave as is
pros: No change at all
cons: The next big button gets sized by hand again, slightly differently

steps.path: Attach a file in the message box → the × on the attachment
steps.headline: The × that removes an attachment is squeezed into a tiny circle by overriding the shared button. Worth fixing?

options.label: Add a small round button
pros: Can fix the too-small tap target on phones at the same time
Reusable for other tiny × buttons
cons: A bigger tap area may need a little more space around the chip

options.label: Leave as is
pros: Looks the same as today
cons: Still hard to tap on a phone

steps.path: Projects → Context tab → How context works
steps.headline: In “How context works”, the timing notes on the right have a hand-typed width, and the arrows a hand-typed indent. Worth fixing?
steps.measured: 210px width and 30px indent, typed in by hand

options.label: Use the spacing scale
pros: Lines up with spacing used across the app
cons: Needs a quick look that the arrows still sit under the icons

options.label: Leave as is
pros: No change
cons: Keeps getting flagged; drifts if the rows change
